questions.text: Select the most grammatically correct and structurally sound version of the following sentence: "Based on the latest inflation data, a rate hike is expected by the Monetary Policy Committee."

options.label: A
options.text: Based on the latest inflation data, a rate hike is expected by the Monetary Policy Committee.

options.label: B
options.text: Basing on the latest inflation data, the Monetary Policy Committee expects a rate hike.

options.label: C
options.text: Based on the latest inflation data, the Monetary Policy Committee expects a rate hike.

options.label: D
options.text: With the latest inflation data as a base, a rate hike is expected by the Monetary Policy Committee.

questions.solution: **Shortcut (Modifier Rule):** An opening participle phrase (e.g., 'Based on...') must modify the grammatical subject of the main clause. Identify the *doer* of the action 'basing'. The MPC bases its decision on data, so 'The Monetary Policy Committee' MUST be the subject immediately following the comma. Eliminate (A) and (D) where 'a rate hike' is the subject. Eliminate (B) because 'Basing on' is unidiomatic; the correct form is 'Based on'. Only (C) satisfies both conditions. **Step-by-Step:** 1. **Identify the Modifier:** The sentence starts with the participle phrase "Based on the latest inflation data". This phrase describes the entity that performed the analysis. 2. **Find the Logical Subject:** Who uses the data as a basis? The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC). Therefore, "The Monetary Policy Committee" must be the subject of the main clause. 3. **Eliminate Dangling Modifiers:** Option (A) and (D) place "a rate hike" as the subject. A rate hike cannot "base itself on data" → Eliminate (A) and (D). 4. **Check Idiomatic Usage:** Option (B) uses "Basing on". Standard English requires the past participle "Based on" (functioning as an adjective) or "Having based". "Basing on" is incorrect → Eliminate (B). 5. **Confirm Correct Option:** Option (C) places the correct subject (MPC) immediately after the modifier and uses the idiomatic "Based on". Active voice ("expects") is preferred over passive ("is expected by").

questions.text: As per the revised Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Commercial Banks effective from 2021, which of the following financial metrics is **NOT** a trigger parameter for invoking PCA?
questions.solution: Shortcut: PCA triggers are strictly *balance-sheet health* indicators (Capital, Asset Quality, Leverage). Profitability (RoA) is a performance metric, not a solvency trigger. Eliminate A, B, C as they are the three explicit risk thresholds. Worked Solution: The RBI revised the PCA framework in 2021 (effective Jan 2022). It monitors three key risk thresholds for triggering mandatory corrective actions: 1) CRAR (Capital), 2) Net NPA Ratio (Asset Quality), and 3) Tier 1 Leverage Ratio (Leverage). While RoA is monitored under the 'Profitability' indicator for discretionary action, it is not a mandatory trigger parameter for PCA invocation.

questions.text: The 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme, launched in September 2023, aims to provide end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople. Which Ministry is the nodal ministry for the implementation of this scheme?

options.label: A
options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)

options.label: B
options.text: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)

questions.solution: Shortcut: The scheme focuses on *skill upgradation*, modern training, and certification of artisans. The Ministry of Skill Development (MSDE) is the logical nodal agency for skill-centric schemes, whereas MSME handles enterprise credit. Worked Solution: PM Vishwakarma was launched on 17th September 2023. It is a Central Sector Scheme fully funded by the Government of India. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) is the nodal ministry. The scheme provides recognition (certificate/ID card), skill upgradation (basic/advanced training), toolkit incentive (Rs 15,000), collateral-free credit support (up to Rs 3 lakh), and market linkage.

questions.text: Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V live on seven different floors of a building, numbered 1 to 7 (1 being the ground floor). Only one person lives on each floor. U lives on floor 4. P lives on an even-numbered floor. There are two floors between P and Q, and Q lives below P. R lives on the floor immediately above S. T lives on an odd-numbered floor above R. V does not live on the topmost floor. Who lives on the 5th floor?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fix U at Floor 4. P must be even (2 or 6). Test P=2 -> Q=5 (2 floors gap). Remaining floors {1,3,6,7} have no consecutive pair for R (immediately above S). Hence P=6, Q=3. Remaining {1,2,5,7}. R/S consecutive only possible at (2,1) -> R=2, S=1. T odd above R(2) -> T=5 or 7. V not on 7 -> V=5, T=7. Answer: V. Full Solution: 1) Place U on Floor 4. 2) P on even floor (2, 6). Case 1: P=2, Q=5. Vacant: 1,3,6,7. R immediately above S requires consecutive floors; none available. Case 1 fails. 3) Case 2: P=6, Q=3. Vacant: 1,2,5,7. R immediately above S fits only at Floors 2(R) and 1(S). 4) T on odd floor above R(2): options 5 or 7. 5) V not on topmost (7), so V=5 and T=7. Final: 7-T, 6-P, 5-V, 4-U, 3-Q, 2-R, 1-S. Person on 5th floor is V.

questions.text: With reference to the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) introduced by the RBI in April 2022, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires banks to pledge Government Securities as collateral.

options.label: B
options.text: It allows banks to park surplus liquidity with RBI without any collateral.

options.label: C
options.text: It is available only to Regional Rural Banks and Small Finance Banks.

options.label: D
options.text: The interest rate on SDF is fixed at 100 basis points above the Policy Repo Rate.

questions.solution: Shortcut: SDF is uniquely defined as a *collateral-free* absorption window. Eliminate Option A (collateral required), Option C (restricted access), and Option D (rate is linked to Repo, not fixed spread above). Worked Solution: The SDF was introduced on April 8, 2022, under Section 17 of the RBI Act. It enables the RBI to absorb liquidity from the banking system without requiring collateral (Government Securities), unlike the Reverse Repo. The SDF rate is set at 25 basis points below the Policy Repo Rate (initially 3.75%), forming the floor of the LAF corridor.

questions.text: In the following question, symbols @, #, $, %, and & are used with the following meanings: 'A @ B' means 'A is not smaller than B'; 'A # B' means 'A is neither smaller than nor equal to B'; 'A $ B' means 'A is neither greater than nor equal to B'; 'A % B' means 'A is not greater than B'; 'A & B' means 'A is neither greater than nor smaller than B'. Statements: P # Q, Q @ R, R $ S, S % T. Conclusions: I. P # R. II. Q $ S. III. R & T.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode symbols: @ => >=, # => >, $ => <, % => <=, & => =. Chain: P > Q >= R < S <= T. Check I: P > Q >= R => P > R (P # R). True. Check II: Q >= R < S. Relation between Q and S unknown (Q could be >, <, or = S). False. Check III: R < S <= T => R < T. R & T means R = T. False. Only I follows. Full Solution: Convert: P > Q; Q >= R; R < S; S <= T. Combine: P > Q >= R < S <= T. Conclusion I: P > R (True, follows #). Conclusion II: Q < S (False, Q >= R < S gives no definite link). Conclusion III: R = T (False, R < T). Only Conclusion I follows.

questions.text: The establishment of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) in 1982 was based on the recommendations of which committee?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Committee-Chairman association is a static GK staple. Sivaraman Committee (1979) -> NABARD. Narasimham Committee -> Banking Sector Reforms (1991, 1998). Rangarajan Committee -> Various (Banking, Statistics, Disinflation). Thorat Committee -> RRB/Cooperative reforms. Worked Solution: The B. Sivaraman Committee was constituted in 1979 to review the institutional credit arrangements for agriculture and rural development. It recommended the establishment of a separate apex development bank for agriculture, leading to the NABARD Act, 1981, and its establishment on 12 July 1982.

questions.text: According to the Logistics Performance Index (LPI) 2023 report released by the World Bank, what was India's rank among 139 countries?
questions.solution: Shortcut: India's rank improved significantly in the 2023 edition (released after a gap due to COVID). Eliminate 44th (India's rank in LPI 2018) and lower ranks (48, 54). The jump to 38th was a highlighted achievement. Worked Solution: The World Bank released the LPI 2023 report titled 'Connecting to Compete'. India ranked 38th out of 139 countries, a significant improvement from 44th in 2018 and 54th in 2014. The improvement was attributed to investments in soft and hard infrastructure, technology adoption (like ICEGATE, E-Sanchit), and policy reforms under PM Gati Shakti.

questions.text: A motorboat covers a certain distance downstream in 4 hours and returns upstream to the starting point in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ratio of Time (Downstream : Upstream) = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3. Since distance is constant, Ratio of Speeds (Downstream : Upstream) = 3 : 2 (inverse ratio). Let Downstream speed = 3x, Upstream speed = 2x. Speed of Boat = (Downstream + Upstream)/2 = (3x + 2x)/2 = 2.5x. Speed of Stream = (Downstream - Upstream)/2 = (3x - 2x)/2 = 0.5x. Ratio Boat : Stream = 2.5x : 0.5x = 5 : 1. Given Stream = 2 km/h, Boat = 5 × 2 = 10 km/h. Full Solution: Let speed of boat = B km/h, stream = 2 km/h. Downstream speed = B+2, Upstream speed = B-2. Distance = Speed × Time. Distance Downstream = 4(B+2). Distance Upstream = 6(B-2). Equating distances: 4(B+2) = 6(B-2) → 4B + 8 = 6B - 12 → 2B = 20 → B = 10 km/h.

questions.text: Under the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement signed between the Government of India and the Reserve Bank of India in February 2015, what is the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation target set for the flexible inflation targeting framework?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall the '4-2-6' rule for the RBI's Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework: Target is 4%, with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (making the upper bound 6% and lower bound 2%). Worked Solution: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (2015) formally adopted Flexible Inflation Targeting. As per the agreement and the subsequent amendment to the RBI Act (2016), the Central Government notified 4% CPI inflation as the target for the period 2016-2021 (extended to 2026), with an upper tolerance limit of 6% and a lower tolerance limit of 2%.

questions.text: A vessel contains 40 litres of pure milk. 4 litres of milk is drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is performed two more times (three times in total). What is the final quantity of milk (in litres) left in the vessel?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the Successive Replacement Formula: Final Quantity = Initial Quantity × (1 - Volume Replaced / Total Volume)^n. Here, Initial = 40, Replaced = 4, Total = 40, n = 3. Milk left = 40 × (1 - 4/40)^3 = 40 × (9/10)^3 = 40 × 729/1000 = 29.16 litres. Full Solution: After 1st operation: Milk = 40 - 4 = 36 L. Concentration = 36/40 = 9/10. After 2nd operation: 4 L of mixture removed contains 4 × (9/10) = 3.6 L milk. Milk left = 36 - 3.6 = 32.4 L. Concentration = 32.4/40 = 0.81. After 3rd operation: 4 L mixture removed contains 4 × 0.81 = 3.24 L milk. Milk left = 32.4 - 3.24 = 29.16 L.

questions.text: A number arrangement machine rearranges an input line of numbers following a particular rule. Input: 48 26 73 19 55 32. Step I: 73 48 26 19 55 32. Step II: 73 55 48 26 19 32. Step III: 73 55 48 32 26 19. Step III is the last step. How many steps will be required for the input: 64 18 92 37 51 29?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Observe Pattern. Input: 48 26 73 19 55 32. Step I: Max (73) moved to Leftmost. Step II: 2nd Max (55) moved to 2nd Left. Step III: 3rd Max (48) already at 3rd? No. Step III: 73 55 48 32 26 19. It's sorting Descending Order from Left. Step I: Pick Max -> Left. Step II: Pick 2nd Max -> 2nd Left. Step III: Pick 3rd Max -> 3rd Left... Wait Step III shows 32 at 4th pos. Actually: Step I: 73 (Max) at 1. Step II: 55 (2nd Max) at 2. Step III: 48 (3rd Max) at 3, 32 (4th Max) at 4, 26 (5th) at 5, 19 (Min) at 6. It completes sorting in 3 steps for 6 numbers? Usually N-1 steps for selection sort. Here Step III is final. Logic: Each step places next highest at correct position from left. New Input: 64 18 92 37 51 29. Sorted Desc: 92 64 51 37 29 18. Step I: 92 (Max) to 1st. [92, 64, 18, 37, 51, 29]. Step II: 64 (2nd Max) already at 2nd? Yes. Machine might still count step or skip? Usually 'Step II: 92 64...' (No change visible but step counted). Step III: 51 (3rd Max) to 3rd. [92, 64, 51, 18, 37, 29]. Step IV: 37 (4th Max) to 4th. [92, 64, 51, 37, 18, 29]. Step V: 29 (5th Max) to 5th. [92, 64, 51, 37, 29, 18]

questions.text: Ten persons are sitting in two parallel rows containing five persons each, with equal distance between adjacent persons. In Row 1, A, B, C, D, and E are seated facing South. In Row 2, P, Q, R, S, and T are seated facing North. Each person in Row 1 faces a person in Row 2. S sits third to the left of P. A faces an immediate neighbor of S. C sits second to the right of A. Only one person sits between B and D. Q and T are immediate neighbors. T does not face A and B. Who amongst the following faces B?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fix Row 2 first using 'S sits third to left of P' -> [S, _, _, P, _] or [_, S, _, _, P]. Since 5 seats, only [S, _, _, P, _] works (S at 1, P at 4). A faces neighbor of S (pos 2). So A is at Row 1 Pos 2. C is 2nd right of A -> C at Row 1 Pos 4. One person between B and D. Remaining Row 1: Pos 1,3,5 for B,D,E. B/D at 1&3 or 3&5. Q,T neighbors in Row 2. Row 2 empty: 2,3,5. Q,T must be 2&3 or 3&5. T not facing A(Pos2) or B. If Q,T at 2,3: T at 3 faces C. If Q,T at 3,5: T at 5 faces E or B/D. Test options: B at Row 1 Pos 3 faces Row 2 Pos 3. Row 2 Pos 3 is Q or T. If T at 3, T faces B (violates 'T not face B'). So Q at 3, T at 2. Q faces B. Full Solution: Row 2: 1-S, 2-T, 3-Q, 4-P, 5-R. Row 1: 1-D, 2-A, 3-B, 4-C, 5-E. B (Pos 3) faces Q (Pos 3).

questions.text: Statements: Only a few Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pens being Erasers is a possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Only a few A are B' = Some A are B + Some A are NOT B. Chain: Some Pens are Pencils -> All Pencils are Erasers -> No Eraser is Sharpener. So Some Pens are Erasers -> No Eraser is Sharpener => Some Pens are not Sharpeners (Definite True). Conclusion I follows. For Possibility: 'All Pens being Erasers' requires the 'Some Pens are NOT Pencils' part to become Erasers. Since Some Pens are Pencils (Erasers) and Some Pens are Not Pencils (Unknown), the rest *can* be Erasers. No statement prohibits Pen=Eraser. So Possibility True. Both follow. Full Solution: Statement 1 gives: Some Pens are Pencils & Some Pens are not Pencils. Statement 2: All Pencils are Erasers. So Some Pens are Erasers. Statement 3: No Eraser is Sharpener. Thus Some Pens are not Sharpeners (I follows). For II: The 'Some Pens are not Pencils' have no relation to Erasers/Sharpeners. They can be Erasers. Hence 'All Pens being Erasers' is a possibility (II follows).

questions.text: Read the sentence divided into four parts (A), (B), (C), and (D) to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Select the part with the error as your answer. (A) Neither the Governor nor the Deputy Governors (B) is expected to attend the meeting (C) scheduled for tomorrow (D) by the central board
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the Proximity Rule for correlative conjunctions 'Neither...Nor'. The verb must agree with the subject nearest to it ('Deputy Governors' - Plural). Scan the verb in Part B ('is' - Singular). It violates the rule. Eliminate Parts A, C, and D as they contain no grammatical faults. The error lies in Part B; 'is' should be 'are'. Full Solution: In 'Neither X nor Y' constructions, the verb agrees with Y (the closer subject). Here, Y is 'Deputy Governors' (Plural). Therefore, the plural verb 'are' is required. Part B incorrectly uses the singular verb 'is'. Parts A, C, and D are grammatically correct.
